latin_text: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Niceph. hist. eccles. lib. 12. cap. 34. Vix triginta annorum spatio et Romanos, et Persas, et Parthos, et Medos, et Indos, et Scythas, et Sauromatas, et Sarracenos, et omne prorsus humanum genus sub jugum mitteret veritatis, &c. Chrysost. homil. 4. de laudib. Pauli. Clemens in epistola ad Corinthios pag. 8. de eodem: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. In oriente ac occidente verbi præco factus, illustrem fidei suæ fainam sortitus est, in justitia mundum universum instruens, et ad occidentis terminos veniens, et sub imperatoribus martyrium subiens, sic e mundo migravit.

translation_history.english: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Nicephorus, Ecclesiastical History, book 12, ch. 34. Within scarcely thirty years' span he would bring under the yoke of truth both the Romans, and the Persians, and the Parthians, and the Medes, and the Indians, and the Scythians, and the Sauromatae, and the Saracens, and altogether the whole human race, etc. Chrysostom, "Homily 4 on the Praises of Paul." Clement, in his epistle to the Corinthians, p. 8, on the same: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. Having become a herald in the East and in the West, he obtained illustrious renown for his faith, instructing the whole world in righteousness, and, coming to the western limits and undergoing martyrdom under the rulers, he thus departed from the world.
translation_history.notes: Both Greek quotations carried through verbatim per Hard Rule #1 (Latin paraphrase 'In oriente ac occidente...' immediately follows the Clement Greek; the Nicephorus Greek is paraphrased in the body text). Latin paraphrases rendered into English. 'fainam' in the source treated as 'famam' (renown), the obvious printer's reading. Treatise title 'de laudibus Pauli' rendered as titled work per Hard Rule #4.
